Chainalysis Hit by Cyberattack, Accessing User Names, Emails, and Organization Roles Blockchain data analytics and tracking firm Chainalysis disclosed that an external hacker used "offensive agentic techniques" to gain unauthorized access to its internal systems and tools, leading to the compromise of some non-sensitive customer data, including user IDs, full names, email addresses, and organization role labels. Chainalysis emphasized in an email that the security incident is unrelated to the recent crypto theft involving Binance. The current investigation has found no indication that investigative content (such as graphs, notes, or cases), transaction or query results, plaintext passwords, MFA secrets, or user session tokens were accessed. The team is actively determining the specific affected records while patching vulnerabilities and hardening system security. — link

ICE Reposts Trade[XYZ] Partnership Announcement, Emphasizing "Plans to Bring" and "Subject to Regulatory Approvals" Following the deletion of its earlier post, Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) reposted its partnership announcement with Trade[XYZ]. In the updated post, ICE amended its phrasing to emphasize that the two parties "plan to bring Hyperliquid-based perps to the U.S." and that operating "U.S. regulated versions" remains strictly "subject to regulatory approvals," with both parties seeking approvals to launch a new market built on Hyperliquid to operate KYC-compliant perp markets, including approvals to support leveraged trading. — link

Binance: 90% of Stolen Assets Replenished; Withdrawals Set to Resume on Nov. 1 Binance announced that it has now replenished 90% of the stolen asset shortfall. The top ten major tokens—including BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD, and ZEC—are now 100% fully backed by reserves. The funding sources for this replenishment include: a partial deployment of the SAFU, reallocated balances from the Futures Insurance Fund exceeding regulatory and risk-management requirements, and Binance’s own corporate treasury. Binance committed to subsequently replenishing SAFU back to approximately US$1 billion. Additionally, the exchange stated that withdrawal services remain on track to resume on November 1 as previously scheduled. According to Arkham on-chain data, Binance's SAFU fund transferred 7,499 BTC, worth approximately $581 million, from wallet 1BAuq to address 165Eur...SMmee at 10:51:41 a.m. EDT on October 31. Binance subsequently confirmed the transfer was complete. — link

Chainalysis: Ethereum Reorg Triggers THORChain Emergency Pause, Delaying Laundering of Binance Hack Funds Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis said an Ethereum chain reorganization on the morning of October 31 (EDT) caused THORChain to mistakenly issue a double refund to a user who had deposited 10 ETH, triggering an emergency pause. The pause blocked cross-chain swaps through most of THORChain’s bridges for all users, including North Korean money launderers, inadvertently delaying the laundering of a significant amount of funds stolen from Binance. — link
